text: Unlike Avocet-7, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Merlin-7 is 3659. Nobody should assume the port of Merlin-7 applies to Avocet-7, the port differs.
Source for Shrike-3 is written in Scala; no other language is allowed in its repository.
Unlike Curlew-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Egret-7 is the Cairo datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Egret-7 applies to Curlew-8, the datacenter differs.
Pages from Plover-4 land on the pager rotation of Mateo Lindqvist before anyone else.
The language of Plover-4 is Elixir, which new contributors must know. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Curlew-8, which is 2850 requests per minute.
Unlike Curlew-8, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Plover-4 is $635k. Nobody should assume the budget of Plover-4 applies to Curlew-8, the budget differs.
The service Plover-4 takes traffic on port 3624, and the port is fixed across every environment.
Egret-7 has one owner, the Ember team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current.
Unlike Egret-7, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Shrike-3 is the Keystone team. Nobody should assume the owner of Shrike-3 applies to Egret-7, the owner differs.
Egret-7 listens on port 7297; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Finance fixed the budget of Egret-7 at $1435k, reviewed every quarter. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Unlike Egret-7, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Avocet-7 is Kotlin. Nobody should assume the language of Avocet-7 applies to Egret-7, the language differs.
Unlike Egret-7, whose budget is handled elsewhere, the budget of Shrike-3 is $1085k. Nobody should assume the budget of Shrike-3 applies to Egret-7, the budget differs.
The retirement date for Shrike-3 is July 19, 2029; after that day it stops serving.
Avocet-7 reaches its retirement date on February 1, 2027, so every consumer has to migrate before then. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The yearly budget for Curlew-8 is $1810k, covering licences and hosting.

Unlike Plover-4, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Shrike-3 is 7262. Nobody should assume the port of Shrike-3 applies to Plover-4, the port differs. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
The yearly budget for Merlin-7 is $440k, covering licences and hosting.
Unlike Curlew-8, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Merlin-7 is the Sprocket team. Nobody should assume the owner of Merlin-7 applies to Curlew-8, the owner differs.
Pages from Avocet-7 land on the pager rotation of Jolene Rasmussen before anyone else.
Curlew-8 is implemented in Erlang; the language was chosen for its tooling. An older draft of this note was archived.
Unlike Merlin-7, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Curlew-8 is the Ember team. Nobody should assume the owner of Curlew-8 applies to Merlin-7, the owner differs.
Unlike Shrike-3, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Avocet-7 is 6080. Nobody should assume the port of Avocet-7 applies to Shrike-3, the port differs.
The language of Egret-7 is Haskell, which new contributors must know. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
The language of Merlin-7 is Go, which new contributors must know.
Plover-4 enforces a rate limit of 150 requests per minute per caller. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Unlike Egret-7, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Curlew-8 is the Perth datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Curlew-8 applies to Egret-7, the datacenter differs.
Merlin-7 enforces a rate limit of 200 requests per minute per caller.
The primary datacenter of Avocet-7 is Osaka; failover is handled by operations.
